1	// Package gitremote provides general-purpose git remote URL utilities:
2	// parsing, resolving, and redacting remote URLs. It has no dependency on
3	// checkpoint, strategy, or settings packages.
4	package gitremote
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"net/url"
11		"os/exec"
12		"strings"
13		"unicode"
14	)
15	
16	const (
17		ProtocolSSH   = "ssh"
18		ProtocolHTTPS = "https"
19		// ProtocolEntire is the scheme of Entire's git remote helper (entire://).
20		// These URLs carry a forge/namespace prefix before owner/repo.
21		ProtocolEntire = "entire"
22	)
23	
24	// Info holds the parsed components of a git remote URL.
25	// Host is the hostname only (never includes a port). Port is empty unless the
26	// source URL specified an explicit non-default port. Callers that need the
27	// combined "host[:port]" form should use HostPort.
28	//
29	// Forge is the short identifier of the upstream forge ("gh", "et", ...) used
30	// by the Entire trails API. It is populated from the path prefix on entire://
31	// URLs (entire://host/<forge>/owner/repo) and from a hostname lookup on
32	// direct git URLs (github.com → "gh"). It is empty for direct git URLs to
33	// unrecognized hosts, and for entire:// URLs without a forge segment.
34	type Info struct {
35		Protocol string
36		Host     string
37		Port     string
38		Forge    string
39		Owner    string
40		Repo     string
41	}
42	
43	// hostToForge maps direct git hostnames to their forge identifier on the
44	// trails API. entire:// URLs carry the forge in the path instead and bypass
45	// this map.
46	var hostToForge = map[string]string{
47		"github.com": "gh",
48	}
49	
50	// forgeToHost is the reverse of hostToForge: it maps a forge identifier back to
51	// its canonical public host. Used to recover the real forge host from an
52	// entire:// remote, whose Host is the Entire cluster rather than the forge.
53	var forgeToHost = func() map[string]string {
54		m := make(map[string]string, len(hostToForge))
55		for host, forge := range hostToForge {
56			m[forge] = host
57		}
58		return m
59	}()
60	
61	// IsSupportedForge reports whether forge is a known short forge id (e.g. "gh")
62	// understood by the trails API. It rejects forge hostnames ("github.com") and
63	// any other unrecognized value, so callers parsing a bare forge/owner/repo
64	// triple can fail clearly instead of forwarding a malformed forge to the API.
65	func IsSupportedForge(forge string) bool {
66		_, ok := forgeToHost[forge]
67		return ok
68	}
69	
70	// CanonicalHost returns the canonical public host of the upstream forge.
71	//
72	// For direct git URLs this is just Host. For entire:// remotes — whose Host is
73	// the Entire cluster (e.g. aws-us-east-2.entire.io) rather than the forge — it
74	// maps the forge prefix back to the forge's host (gh → github.com). Falls back
75	// to Host when the forge is unknown (e.g. a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise),
76	// preserving the only host we know for it.
77	func (i *Info) CanonicalHost() string {
78		if host, ok := forgeToHost[i.Forge]; ok {
79			return host
80		}
81		return i.Host
82	}
83	
84	// HostPort returns Host, or "Host:Port" when Port is non-empty.
85	func (i *Info) HostPort() string {
86		if i.Port == "" {
87			return i.Host
88		}
89		return i.Host + ":" + i.Port
90	}
91	
92	// GetRemoteURL returns the URL configured for the named git remote.
93	func GetRemoteURL(ctx context.Context, remoteName string) (string, error) {
94		return GetRemoteURLInDir(ctx, "", remoteName)
95	}
96	
97	// GetRemoteURLInDir returns the URL configured for the named git remote in dir.
98	func GetRemoteURLInDir(ctx context.Context, dir, remoteName string) (string, error) {
99		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "remote", "get-url", remoteName)
100		if dir != "" {
101			cmd.Dir = dir
102		}
103		output, err := cmd.Output()
104		if err != nil {
105			return "", fmt.Errorf("remote %q not found", remoteName)
106		}
107		return strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), nil
108	}
109	
110	// GetPushURLs returns every URL a push to remoteName delivers to, in the order
111	// git will use them.
112	//
113	// A remote's push destinations are remote.<name>.pushurl when any is set and its
114	// remote.<name>.url otherwise (git's push_url_of_remote), and BOTH may repeat —
115	// git pushes to all of them, in config order. So this, not GetRemoteURL,
116	// describes where a push actually goes; GetRemoteURL reports the FETCH URL,
117	// which can name a different repository entirely.
118	//
119	// Returns at least one entry on success.
120	func GetPushURLs(ctx context.Context, remoteName string) ([]string, error) {
121		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "remote", "get-url", "--push", "--all", remoteName)
122		output, err := cmd.Output()
123		if err != nil {
124			return nil, fmt.Errorf("remote %q not found", remoteName)
125		}
126		var urls []string
127		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(output), "\n") {
128			if trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line); trimmed != "" {
129				urls = append(urls, trimmed)
130			}
131		}
132		if len(urls) == 0 {
133			return nil, fmt.Errorf("remote %q has no push URL", remoteName)
134		}
135		return urls, nil
136	}

138	// GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet returns every raw URL stored for the named git
139	// remote in dir, distinguishing "remote not configured" from a failed lookup:
140	// exit code 1 from `git config --get-all` is reported as found=false with a
141	// nil error — for well-formed remote names that means the key is unset (git
142	// also exits 1 for invalid key names). Any other failure (dir missing, git
143	// unavailable, context canceled) returns an error. `git remote get-url`
144	// could make the same distinction — its failures are distinguishable too
145	// (exit 2 for "no such remote" vs 128 for not-a-repo) — but
146	// it is deliberately not used, for two reasons: (i) it expands
147	// url.<base>.insteadOf rewrites, which would break the ExcludeOrigins
148	// contract that patterns match what git config STORES
149	// (settings.GlobalConfig.ExcludeOrigins — a stored gh:acme/widgets must not
150	// come back as git@github.com:acme/widgets), and (ii) `git config
151	// --get-all` gives the clean exit-1-means-unset contract this function's
152	// found return is built on. A remote can carry several fetch URLs (git
153	// remote set-url --add); callers matching for exclusion should treat a
154	// match on ANY of them as a match.
155	//
156	// The lookup deliberately reads EFFECTIVE config (no --local): git itself
157	// builds a repo's remotes from the full config stack, so a remote defined in
158	// global/system scope IS that repo's origin (git remote -v lists it and
159	// fetch uses it). Scoping to --local would make origin exclusion diverge
160	// from git's own view, treating such a repo as origin-less.
161	func GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet(ctx context.Context, dir, remoteName string) (urls []string, found bool, err error) {
162		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "config", "--get-all", "remote."+remoteName+".url")
163		if dir != "" {

175			if line = strings.TrimSpace(line); line != "" {

182	// ParseURL parses a git remote URL (SSH SCP-style or HTTPS) into its components.
183	func ParseURL(rawURL string) (*Info, error) {
184		rawURL = strings.TrimSpace(rawURL)
185	
186		if strings.Contains(rawURL, ":") && !strings.Contains(rawURL, "://") {
187			parts := strings.SplitN(rawURL, ":", 2)
188			if len(parts) != 2 {
189				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid SSH URL: %s", RedactURL(rawURL))
190			}
191	
192			hostPart := parts[0]
193			_, host, found := strings.Cut(hostPart, "@")
194			if !found {
195				host = hostPart
196			}
197	
198			pathPart := strings.TrimSuffix(parts[1], ".git")
199			owner, repo, err := splitOwnerRepo(pathPart)
200			if err != nil {
201				return nil, err
202			}
203	
204			return &Info{Protocol: ProtocolSSH, Host: host, Forge: hostToForge[host], Owner: owner, Repo: repo}, nil
205		}
206	
207		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
208		if err != nil {
209			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid URL: %s", RedactURL(rawURL))
210		}
211		if u.Scheme == "" {
212			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no protocol in URL: %s", RedactURL(rawURL))
213		}
214	
215		pathPart := strings.TrimPrefix(u.Path, "/")
216		forge := hostToForge[u.Hostname()]
217		if u.Scheme == ProtocolEntire {
218			// entire:// URLs encode the forge as the first path segment.
219			forge, pathPart = splitForgePrefix(pathPart)
220		}
221		owner, repo, err := splitOwnerRepo(pathPart)
222		if err != nil {
223			return nil, err
224		}
225	
226		return &Info{Protocol: u.Scheme, Host: u.Hostname(), Port: u.Port(), Forge: forge, Owner: owner, Repo: repo}, nil
227	}
228	
229	// splitForgePrefix returns the leading forge/namespace segment of an entire://
230	// URL path and the remainder (e.g. "gh/owner/repo" -> "gh", "owner/repo").
231	// Paths without a separator are returned with an empty forge.
232	func splitForgePrefix(path string) (forge, rest string) {
233		if forge, rest, found := strings.Cut(path, "/"); found {
234			return forge, rest
235		}
236		return "", path
237	}
238	
239	// RedactURL removes credentials and query parameters from a URL for safe logging.
240	// SCP-style SSH URLs (e.g., git@github.com:org/repo.git) are returned as-is
241	// since they contain no embedded credentials.
242	func RedactURL(rawURL string) string {
243		// SCP-style SSH: user@host:path — no credentials to redact.
244		if strings.Contains(rawURL, ":") && !strings.Contains(rawURL, "://") {
245			return rawURL
246		}
247	
248		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
249		if err != nil {
250			return "<unparseable>"
251		}
252		u.User = nil
253		u.RawQuery = ""
254		return u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host + u.Path
255	}
256	
257	// RedactURLOrPath renders a remote for display with any credentials removed,
258	// accepting values that are not URLs at all.
259	//
260	// RedactURL cannot be applied blanket-fashion: it round-trips through url.Parse
261	// and rebuilds "scheme://host/path", so a bare filesystem path like
262	// /srv/repo.git comes back as ":///srv/repo.git" and a bare word like "origin"
263	// as "://origin". Those inputs carry no credentials, so they pass through
264	// unchanged. Use this wherever the value may be a remote name, a local path, or
265	// a URL — i.e. anywhere a push/fetch target is shown to a user.
266	func RedactURLOrPath(remote string) string {
267		if strings.Contains(remote, "://") || strings.Contains(remote, "@") {
268			return RedactURL(remote)
269		}
270		return remote
271	}
272	
273	// ResolveRemoteRepo returns the forge identifier, owner, and repo name for the
274	// given git remote. The forge is the short id used by the trails API ("gh",
275	// "et", ...); it is derived from the hostname for direct git URLs or from the
276	// path prefix on entire:// URLs. It is empty for unrecognized hosts.
277	// For example, git@github.com:org/my-repo.git returns ("gh", "org", "my-repo").
278	func ResolveRemoteRepo(ctx context.Context, remoteName string) (forge, owner, repo string, err error) {
279		rawURL, err := GetRemoteURL(ctx, remoteName)
280		if err != nil {
281			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("get remote URL for %q: %w", remoteName, err)
282		}
283		info, err := ParseURL(rawURL)
284		if err != nil {
285			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("parse remote URL: %w", err)
286		}
287		return info.Forge, info.Owner, info.Repo, nil
288	}
289	
290	func splitOwnerRepo(path string) (string, string, error) {
291		path = strings.TrimSuffix(path, ".git")
292		parts := strings.SplitN(path, "/", 2)
293		if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
294			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("cannot parse owner/repo from path: %s", path)
295		}
296		// Reject control characters (newlines, ANSI escapes, ...). The SCP-style
297		// branch in ParseURL bypasses net/url.Parse's built-in control-char
298		// rejection, so a crafted origin URL could otherwise smuggle a newline or
299		// escape into owner/repo and, via plain-text consumers like `entire
300		// agent-help`, into an agent's context or a user's terminal. This shared
301		// chokepoint protects every caller; the tainted bytes are not echoed back.
302		if strings.IndexFunc(parts[0]+"/"+parts[1], unicode.IsControl) >= 0 {
303			return "", "", errors.New("invalid control character in remote owner/repo")
304		}
305		return parts[0], parts[1], nil
306	}
